newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Bees disrupt genital mutilation in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Bees disrupt genital mutilation in Sierra Leone.

text.p: Thousands of bees disrupted a female circumcision ceremony in Sierra Leone, putting half the 100 girls taking part in hospital, one of the girls said.
Hospital sources said that most of the girls stung by bees during the ceremony in the northern region capital of Makeni on Wednesday had been discharged after receiving treatment.
The bees prevented some of Wednesday's planned circumcisions taking place but some girls who had been mutilated were also being treated for serious bleeding and fever, they added.

"Bees in their thousands attacked the girls and the leaders of the traditional practice," Kadiatu Conteh told Reuters. "The bees attacked us again and again leaving our half naked bodies battered and our faces and eyes swollen."
Sierra Leone has one of the highest rates of female circumcision in Africa -- up to 90 percent of all its women.
The practice, which consists of slicing off a girl's labia and clitoris, has been widely condemned on health grounds.
